subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Volkswagen Beetle
description: A fast breakdown of The Volkswagen Beetle for builders.

hook.text: The Beetle was designed in the 1930s and stayed in production for 65 years. Nothing else comes close.

buildup.text: Its air-cooled flat-four engine was simple, cheap to repair, and reliable in almost any climate.

discovery.text: After WWII, the British Army got the Wolfsburg factory running. The Beetle spread to every continent.

twist.text: In America, DDB's 'Think Small' ad campaign turned the Beetle into a countercultural icon.

climax.text: Over 21.5 million were built—the best-selling single car design in history for decades.

punchline.text: Simplicity was the Beetle's greatest engineering feat.

quiz.question: How many years was the Beetle in production?

details.summary: The Volkswagen Beetle, originally designed as Hitler's people's car, became an ironic symbol of peace and individuality, selling over 21 million units and earning a permanent place in automotive history.
details.whyItMatters: The Beetle's journey from Nazi propaganda project to global icon of freedom demonstrates how a car's meaning is ultimately defined by its owners, not its creators.
takeaways: Ferdinand Porsche designed it under commission from Adolf Hitler
Over 21 million were produced from 1938 to 2003
It became the counterculture car of the 1960s in America

faq.question: How did the Beetle survive its Nazi origins?
faq.answer: British Army officer Ivan Hirst restarted production in 1945 to create jobs in occupied Germany. Brilliant advertising by DDB in the 1960s repositioned it as honest, humble, and anti-establishment.

faq.question: Why was the Beetle discontinued?
faq.answer: The air-cooled rear engine design could not meet modern safety and emissions standards. VW launched a New Beetle in 1998 on a Golf platform, but the final version was discontinued in 2019 as SUVs dominated sales.
